features.name: Page Background Tasks
features.description: A mechanism for loading field values and page calculations asynchronously after the page opens, preventing delays to page opening procedures. Read-only by design, session-specific, with separate error handling and page object integration.
caveats: read-only by design
not schedulable
does not survive server restarts
session cancelled if record changed or page closed
not suitable for list pages
deeply integrated on page objects only
only works for field calculations on pages

features.name: Start Session
features.description: The oldest background processing mechanism built as the foundation for other background tasks. Allows running codeunits in another session with read and write capabilities but no error logging or scheduling. Can be started anywhere in code.
caveats: no scheduling capability
no error logging
no error handling
limited to codeunits only
cancelled if server crashes
runs on same server instance and user context
limited parameters - can only specify another company
runs in same user context

features.name: Task Scheduler
features.description: A background processing mechanism built on top of start session that adds data writing capability, one-time scheduling, failure codeunit for error handling, and server restart persistence. Backed by scheduled tasks table and works across server instances.
caveats: no logging out of the box
not user configurable
one-time scheduling only
backed by table called schedule tasks
worker picks up tasks across server instances

features.name: Job Queue
features.description: The most complete background processing mechanism with recurring scheduling, automatic logging, and a user interface for configuration and management. Built on top of task scheduler. Includes locking capability and job queue dispatcher.
caveats: user interface not great for general users
requires knowledgeable users
dialogue confirms and errors are suppressed
recurring jobs can fail silently

features.name: Job Queue Categories
features.description: Organizational feature for job queue entries that allows grouping and filtering of tasks. Prevents heavy processes from blocking other job queue entries by enabling parallel processing of different workload types.

features.name: Job Queue Record ID and Parameter String
features.description: Job queue entries support specifying a record ID to process and a parameter string, enabling flexible processing of specific records and passing data through the queuing mechanism.
caveats: Parameter string described as a hack but works effectively

features.name: Job Queue Error Handling
features.description: Job queue entries that fail to process are recorded with error messages, allowing selective error handling and preventing one failed entry from blocking other entries in the queue.

features.name: Task Scheduler Failure Handler
features.description: Error handling mechanism for scheduled tasks that captures error context including error text and call stack, logs failures to execution log table with status, allowing reactions to task failures.

features.name: Multi-Level Job Queue Workflows
features.description: Job queue entries can trigger other job queue entries in sequence, enabling complex multi-step workflows where invoice creation triggers posting and posting triggers payment processing.

features.name: Warehouse Request Architecture
features.description: A deferred warehouse processing approach where the system creates a warehouse request on order release instead of immediately creating picks, allowing the warehouse activity creation to run asynchronously.
caveats: Only applies when warehousing functionality is enabled

features.name: Production order asynchronous planning
features.description: A design pattern that offloads production order planning to a background job queue entry rather than executing synchronously during order release, improving perceived performance for users.
caveats: depends on warehouse request creation flow
requires production order planning request table

features.name: Business Central Online Compute Node Distribution
features.description: Business Central online runs 99.81% of sessions on compute-only nodes (NSTs) that do not host user sessions, allowing background tasks and job queues to execute on dedicated infrastructure.
caveats: Quote appears to have transcription error with 99.81% and 81%

features.name: Automatic NST Scaling
features.description: Business Central online automatically spins up new compute nodes (NSTs) when existing nodes reach capacity thresholds, distributing sessions across multiple nodes to balance load.

features.name: Session Limit - Start Session
features.description: Business Central online has a limit of 5 background sessions actively running per user and can queue up to 100 sessions per user in the cloud.
caveats: Speaker notes this is most recent information and recommends checking documentation
Changed from per-tenant/per-environment to per-user model

features.name: Auto-Scaling Limited to Task Scheduler and Job Queue
features.description: Auto-scaling on multiple NSTs applies only to task scheduler and job queue usage, not to page background tasks which run on the same NST.
caveats: Page background tasks and start session always run on same NST as the page

features.name: Page Background Tasks for API Calls
features.description: Discussion of using page background tasks to handle slow API calls. Guidance indicates this approach works for read-only API calls but may cause issues with write operations if tasks get cancelled.
caveats: should only be used for read operations
write operations may encounter issues if tasks are cancelled
blog post mentioned but not fully endorsed
